en.name: JSON Compare
en.description: Compare two JSON documents online and identify added, removed, and changed data. This browser-based JSON compare tool performs a structural comparison of objects and arrays, highlights differences by category, and helps you inspect changes by JSON path.

hero.trustHtml: Runs in your browser. Your JSON is not uploaded by this tool.

meta.title: JSON Compare – Free Online JSON Diff Tool
meta.description: Compare two JSON documents online with a structural JSON diff. Find added, removed, and changed keys and values, sort keys, optionally ignore array order, and review differences in your browser.

features.title: Structural JSON Comparison
features.description: Compare parsed JSON objects and arrays by structure and value instead of treating formatting or whitespace as meaningful differences.

features.title: Side-by-Side Diff View
features.description: Review the original and modified JSON next to each other while the result identifies differences between the two documents.

features.title: Added, Removed, and Changed
features.description: Separate differences into added, removed, and changed data so you can quickly identify what was introduced, deleted, or modified.

features.title: Nested Path Context
features.description: Show where a difference occurs within the JSON structure, such as user.profile.name or items[2].price, when path information is available in the comparison result.

features.title: Comparison Options
features.description: Sort object keys before comparison and optionally ignore array order when the position of array items is not meaningful for your data.

features.title: Swap Inputs
features.description: Swap the original and modified documents to reverse the comparison direction and review additions and removals from the other perspective.

features.title: Paste or Open JSON
features.description: Paste two JSON documents or open local JSON files when file input is available. Both documents are parsed in the browser before comparison.

features.title: Browser-Based Comparison
features.description: JSON parsing and comparison happen in your browser. The page does not require an account or upload the source documents to a comparison server.

guide.title: Enter the original JSON
guide.description: Paste the baseline or original document into JSON A. This is the version used as the starting point for classifying added, removed, and changed values.

guide.title: Enter the modified JSON
guide.description: Paste the newer or comparison document into JSON B. The tool compares this document against JSON A.

guide.title: Configure comparison rules
guide.description: Sort object keys when key order should not matter, and enable Ignore array order only when the array represents an unordered collection.

guide.title: Compare and inspect
guide.description: Click Compare to parse both documents and inspect the difference categories, paths, values, and structure shown by the result.

guide.title: Swap or copy the result
guide.description: Swap the inputs to reverse the comparison direction, then copy the relevant output or use the displayed differences in debugging, testing, documentation, or code review.

faq.question: Does this compare JSON semantically or as plain text?
faq.answer: The intended comparison is structural: both inputs are parsed as JSON, so whitespace and formatting should not count as data changes. Object key order can also be normalized when Sort Keys is enabled or when the comparison engine treats object order as insignificant.

faq.question: What types of differences can it detect?
faq.answer: It can classify properties or array values as added, removed, or changed. A type change, such as a number becoming a string or an object becoming an array, should be treated as a changed value or structure according to the comparison result.

faq.question: Does it compare nested objects and arrays?
faq.answer: Yes. The comparison is recursive for nested JSON objects and arrays. The exact array result depends on whether items are compared by position or by an order-independent rule.

faq.question: What does Sort Keys do?
faq.answer: Sort Keys normalizes the order of object properties before comparison. This prevents a different property order from being reported as a meaningful data change. It does not sort array items.

faq.question: What does Ignore array order do?
faq.answer: It treats array position as less important when the array represents an unordered collection. The matching algorithm must still determine how duplicate or similar items are paired, so use this option carefully for arrays containing repeated or partially changed objects.

faq.question: Are arrays compared by index?
faq.answer: By default, arrays are commonly compared by position, so inserting an item near the beginning can cause later indexes to appear changed. If the data is an unordered collection, enable Ignore array order only when that behavior matches your data model.

faq.question: Can I compare JSON files with different sizes?
faq.answer: Yes. The documents do not need to contain the same number of properties, rows, or nested levels. Missing properties are reported as removed or added according to the selected comparison direction.

faq.question: Can I compare minified and formatted JSON?
faq.answer: Yes, provided both inputs are valid JSON. Formatting, indentation, and whitespace should not affect a structural comparison.

faq.question: Can I compare numbers and strings with similar values?
faq.answer: A structural comparator should distinguish JSON types. For example, the number 1 and the string "1" are different values even though they look similar when displayed.

faq.question: Can I reverse the comparison?
faq.answer: Yes. Use Swap to exchange JSON A and JSON B. This reverses which document is treated as the original and which is treated as the modified version, so additions and removals are viewed from the opposite direction.

faq.question: Can I load JSON from a URL?
faq.answer: This page is designed primarily for pasted JSON and local file input. Loading arbitrary URLs may fail because of CORS restrictions and may expose remote or private data to the browser. Add URL loading only with appropriate validation and security controls.

faq.question: Can I compare large JSON documents?
faq.answer: The practical limit depends on browser memory, device performance, document depth, array size, and the complexity of the diff result. Large comparisons may take longer and may require a more compact result view.

faq.question: Is my JSON uploaded to a server?
faq.answer: This page is designed to parse and compare both documents in your browser without requiring a server upload. You should still avoid entering passwords, API keys, access tokens, private customer data, or confidential production payloads into any browser-based tool.

faq.question: Is this a free JSON compare tool?
faq.answer: Yes. You can enter two JSON documents, compare their structure and values, and inspect the differences without creating an account.

ui.status_identical: The JSON documents are structurally identical
ui.error_invalid_a: JSON A is not valid JSON
ui.error_invalid_b: JSON B is not valid JSON

article.title: How to Compare JSON Files Online
article.content:
What Is a JSON Compare Tool?

A JSON compare tool examines two JSON documents and reports how their structure and values differ. It is useful when you need to compare API responses, configuration files, test fixtures, exported data, or two versions of a payload.

A structural JSON comparison parses the documents before comparing them. This means formatting, indentation, and whitespace do not normally count as changes. The result can focus on meaningful data differences such as added properties, removed properties, changed values, and type changes.

Common Use Cases

  • API debugging: Compare expected and actual responses to locate missing fields, changed values, or unexpected types.
  • Configuration review: Compare environment-specific files or old and new configuration versions.
  • Data migration: Check whether records changed during an export, import, or transformation.
  • Regression testing: Compare snapshot outputs, test fixtures, or serialized results.
  • Code review: Review JSON payload changes without manually scanning two large documents.
  • Webhook and event debugging: Compare two event payloads to identify changes in nested properties or metadata.

How to Compare Two JSON Documents

  1. Enter JSON A: Paste the original or baseline document into the first editor.
  2. Enter JSON B: Paste the modified or newer document into the second editor.
  3. Choose normalization options: Sort object keys when property order should not matter. Use Ignore array order only when array position is semantically irrelevant.
  4. Run the comparison: Click Compare JSON to parse and compare both inputs.
  5. Review the result: Inspect added, removed, and changed values together with their paths and old or new values when available.
  6. Reverse the view if needed: Use Swap inputs to treat JSON B as the original and JSON A as the modified version.

Added, Removed, and Changed Values

  • Added: A property or array value appears in JSON B but not in JSON A.
  • Removed: A property or array value appears in JSON A but not in JSON B.
  • Changed: A property exists in both documents but its value, type, or nested structure differs.
  • Identical: Both documents represent the same data under the selected normalization rules.

Structural Diff vs Text Diff

A text diff compares lines and characters. It may show many changes when a JSON document is only reformatted or when object properties are reordered. A structural diff parses JSON first and compares objects, arrays, values, and types. This is usually more useful when the question is whether the data changed rather than whether the text changed.

Text diffs are still useful when whitespace, formatting, comments in JSON-like formats, or exact source representation matters. Choose the comparison method that matches the question you are trying to answer.

Object Key Order and Array Order

Object properties are generally treated as named fields, so their order should not determine whether two JSON objects contain the same data. Sorting keys can make this behavior explicit. Arrays are different: their order may be meaningful, such as a ranked list, timeline, or ordered set of steps.

Do not enable Ignore array order simply to reduce the number of differences. Use it only when the array represents an unordered collection. Matching arrays without order can also be ambiguous when several items are identical or have similar fields.

Type Changes Matter

JSON values have different types. The number 1, the string "1", the boolean true, the null value null, an object, and an array are not interchangeable. A useful comparator should report type changes because they can break API clients, validation rules, calculations, and application logic.

Reading JSON Paths

A difference path identifies where a change occurs. Examples include user.name, settings.timeout, or items[2].price. Paths help you move from a high-level statement such as “the payload changed” to the exact property that needs review.

Comparing API Responses

When comparing API responses, normalize values that are intentionally dynamic, such as timestamps, request IDs, pagination tokens, or generated trace IDs. If the tool does not support ignored paths, remove or preprocess those fields before comparison. Otherwise, expected runtime differences may obscure meaningful changes.

Limitations of JSON Comparison

  • Array matching: Order-independent comparison requires a matching strategy and can be ambiguous for duplicate objects.
  • Large documents: Recursive parsing and a detailed diff can require substantial browser memory.
  • Dynamic fields: Timestamps, IDs, and randomized values may create differences that are not defects.
  • JSON only: Comments, trailing commas, and JSON5 syntax are not valid standard JSON unless a separate parser is provided.
  • Semantic meaning: A diff identifies structural and value changes but cannot determine whether a change is correct for your business logic.

Browser-Based Privacy

This comparison tool is designed to parse both JSON documents in the browser rather than sending them to a remote comparison service. That can be useful for development payloads and private configuration samples. It is not a substitute for secure secret handling, so avoid entering credentials, tokens, private customer information, or production secrets into any online tool.

Local Alternatives

For automated testing, CI pipelines, very large files, or confidential data, consider a local command-line or programming-library workflow. Tools such as jq can normalize JSON before a standard diff, while application-specific test libraries can compare selected fields or ignore known dynamic paths.

faq.answer: 支持。比较是递归的，可以处理深度嵌套的 JSON 对象和数组。你可以比较任意嵌套层级的 JSON，并查看结构中的每个差异。

faq.question: 可以复制或导出差异结果吗？

faq.question: 差异中的颜色代表什么？
faq.answer: 通常，新增的键或值会用绿色标记，删除的项用红色标记，修改的值用黄色或其他高亮颜色标记。具体配色可能略有差异，但界面中的说明或标签会指示每种颜色对应的变更类型。

article.title: 如何在线比较 JSON 文件并查找差异
article.content:
为什么要比较 JSON？

比较 JSON 文档对于调试 API、验证配置更改和确保数据完整性非常重要。无论是在检查 API 响应、比较配置文件版本，还是验证数据迁移结果，JSON 差异工具都能帮助你快速、准确地发现每个差异。

常见使用场景

  • API 调试：比较预期与实际 API 响应，查找字段缺失、值错误或结构变化等问题
  • 配置更改：跟踪不同版本配置文件之间的差异，或对比不同环境的配置
  • 数据迁移：验证数据是否在系统或数据库之间正确传输，没有遗漏或错误
  • 代码审查：在 Pull Request 中比较 JSON 负载，确认改动是否符合预期
  • 测试与回归：比较测试用例的 JSON 输出或快照，检测回归和意外变更

如何在线比较 JSON

  1. 粘贴 JSON A：将原始 JSON 文档添加到左侧面板。
  2. 粘贴 JSON B：将修改后的 JSON 文档添加到右侧面板。
  3. 点击比较：运行比较，分析两个文档的差异。
  4. 查看结果：新增、删除和修改的键与值会以颜色标记，方便快速识别。
  5. 导出结果（可选）：复制差异内容或下载为报告，用于问题记录、文档或团队沟通。

理解差异结果

  • 新增（绿色）：在 JSON B 中存在但在 JSON A 中不存在的键或值
  • 删除（红色）：在 JSON A 中存在但在 JSON B 中缺失的键或值
  • 修改（黄色/高亮）：在两个文档中都存在，但值或类型发生变化的键

嵌套对象和数组会递归比较，因此深层结构中的差异也会被检测并高亮显示。

最佳实践

  • 先格式化：使用 JSON 格式化工具确保两个文档可读，再进行比较。
  • 检查整体结构：如果两个 JSON 的整体结构差异很大，可能会产生大量变更提示，此时可以分步比较中间版本。
  • 导出结果：将差异结果复制到剪贴板或下载为报告，便于在问题报告、文档或代码审查中使用。
  • 利用 URL 输入：在支持时，直接通过 URL 比较远程 API 响应，减少复制粘贴的步骤。
  • 逐步对比：对于复杂变更，可以比较多个中间版本，理解数据是如何逐步演化的。

浏览器本地处理与隐私

这个 JSON 比较工具在浏览器中处理输入内容，不要求将数据上传到远程服务。对于开发数据和私密配置片段来说，本地处理更加方便。不过，仍然不建议在任何浏览器工具中输入密码、API 密钥、访问令牌或其他高度敏感的信息。
